items.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But Howell Epps was just a guy that lived in the neighborhood and he had a saxophone.

ctx.x: -- no. It was just in Newark. We didn't go to the same school. You see, if I was walking down the street anywhere and I heard a saxophone playing out a window, I'd go knock on the door. I mean, in those days, it was funny. People did things like that, you know. But Howell Epps was just a guy that lived in the neighborhood and he had a saxophone. You know, and so.
